name: Future Trauma Surgeon Joel Mutyaba Living his Purpose

content.title: Future Trauma Surgeon Joel Mutyaba Living his Purpose
content.summary: Joel Mutyaba is determined to become a trauma surgeon & innovative healthcare entrepreneur

content.text: Joel Mutyaba, a SONAM EA graduand from Uganda, is a dedicated healthcare worker, entrepreneur and family man. While pursuing his diploma in nursing, Joel was working at Kibuli Hospital while managing his business, Salem Medical Clinic. His story reflects a careful balancing act between pursuing his nursing career, nurturing his entrepreneurial spirit, and making time for personal growth by being part of AKU's graduating class of 2024.

"It's not easy," Joel admits. "Sometimes I feel like there aren't enough hours in the day." However, he credits his ability to juggle these responsibilities to his deep passion for both medicine and entrepreneurship. His clinic, which offers primary healthcare services to underserved communities, is not just a business for him but an extension of his commitment to improving healthcare in Uganda.

Joel's success is also thanks to the strong support system he has found at AKU. The university's nurturing environment, including the guidance of faculty and staff, as well as the camaraderie among fellow students, plays a vital role in his ability to manage his dual roles. "The support from my professors and classmates has been incredible," Joel shares. "Someone is always listening. When I'm overwhelmed, I know I can turn to them for advice, encouragement, or even just a little moral support."

SONAM EA's approach to health sciences goes beyond just theory; it focuses on developing well-rounded healthcare professionals with practical skills. For Joel, this approach is invaluable. "It's not just about learning from books. We get hands-on experience that prepares us for real-world medical challenges," he says. From interacting with patients to performing minor procedures under supervision, Joel is gaining the practical skills necessary for his future role as a surgeon.

One of the aspects Joel appreciates most about AKU is the flexibility of its student policies. "Being a working student can be tough, but the faculty is understanding," he explains. The university offers flexible learning options and a supportive academic environment that allows students like Joel to balance their education with other commitments.

Joel also values the mentorship he receives from faculty members. "The professors are always available to offer guidance, whether it's about coursework or my future career plans," he notes. This mentorship has been crucial in helping Joel refine his goals, from excelling in his studies to becoming a trauma surgeon and healthcare entrepreneur.

Joel's long-term goal is to specialize in trauma surgery, a field that excites him due to its fast-paced, high-impact nature. "I want to be the surgeon who can make a difference when every second counts," he says passionately. Joel plans to pursue further specialization in trauma and emergency surgery after completing his diploma. His ultimate vision is to work in both private and public sectors, contributing to Uganda's healthcare system and saving lives in critical situations.

In addition to his medical aspirations, Joel is also passionate about healthcare entrepreneurship. He currently runs Salem Medical Clinic, which offers a range of medical services, including basic healthcare, diagnostics, and treatment for common ailments. Looking ahead, Joel plans to expand his clinic into a network of healthcare centers, providing more comprehensive services to underserved areas. "Healthcare is a huge need in Uganda, and I want to be part of the solution," he shares.
